You check whether a knowledge-base article answers a support ticket for a clinical practice-management product. Set answers_ticket to true only if following the article would resolve what the ticket actually asks. An article about a related task does not answer it: an article on placing an order does not answer a question about cancelling one. If the ticket asks for more than one thing, the article must answer all of them: an article that covers only part of the request does not answer it. Give the reason in one sentence.

Reply with only a JSON object and no other text.
Output: grounding.
The JSON object must match this JSON schema:
{"additionalProperties": false, "description": "Whether the best-matching article actually answers the ticket.", "properties": {"answers_ticket": {"title": "Answers Ticket", "type": "boolean"}, "reason": {"minLength": 1, "title": "Reason", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["answers_ticket", "reason"], "title": "grounding", "type": "object"}

Article id: configure-roles-and-permissions
Article: Assign user roles and configure permission levels
Protect sensitive clinical and financial data by tailoring access for your staff. Only practice managers and primary administrators can modify security credentials.

1. Go to **Settings > Practice Staff > Roles & Permissions**.
2. Click **Create New Role** or select an existing title from the directory.
3. Toggle permissions across categories, including *Billing*, *Patient Charts*, and *System Settings*.
4. Click **Assign Users**, select the staff members who require this profile, and click **Save Changes**.

**Limits & Conditions:** Every active user profile must be assigned to at least one role. Direct permission overrides on individual accounts are not permitted; all restrictions must flow through the assigned role.

**Troubleshooting:** If a staff member cannot view a restricted menu after saving, verify their account status is active and have them clear their browser cache before logging back in.

Ticket:
Adjusting staff permission tiers for financial data

Hello, I am reviewing our current user access settings and would like to set up some custom security roles for our administrative team. We need to make sure that front desk staff cannot view sensitive payroll and financial records while still retaining scheduling access. Could someone walk me through the best way to structure these permission levels in our enterprise account? Thank you.
